newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 96 TRADE GAP DOUBLES TO $12.6 BLN -MINISTRY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 96 TRADE GAP DOUBLES TO $12.6 BLN -MINISTRY.

text.p: Poland's registered trade deficit soared to $12.6 billion zlotys last year from $6.16 billion in 1995, preliminary Economy Ministry figures showed.

The ministry's analysis department said that exports, counted by customs receipts and not current account cash flow, increased by 6.3 percent to $24.35 billion in 1996 and imports jumped 27.2 percent to $36.94 billion.
It said that exports to the European Union (EU) edged up 0.7 percent last year to $16.15 billion, while imports rose 25.6 percent to 23.59 billion.
Exports to Germany, Poland's largest trading partner, fell by 4.8 percent last year and amounted to $8.35 billion, while imports increased by 17.5 percent to $9.09 billion.
The National Bank of Poland, which counts merchandise trade by current account flows, said that during the January-November period of last year Poland had a $7.2 billion trade deficit.
The ministry said that unregistered cross-border trade inflows, which largely neutralise the large official trade deficit, amounted to $6-$8 billion last year.
